candidate.name: delaney-esol-scaffold-evaluation
candidate.description: Use the Delaney ESOL molecular-solubility dataset with its measured label and a scaffold split when evaluating structure-based solubility models.
candidate.operation: load the bundled Delaney CSV, identify SMILES and measured log-solubility labels, then choose a scaffold split for model evaluation

inputs.text: A Delaney CSV containing SMILES structures and measured log solubility labels.

citations.quote: SMILES representation of the molecular structure

outputs.text: Features and regression labels, optionally divided into train, validation and test sets.

steps.text: Read the bundled CSV using the smiles feature field and the measured log-solubility task; use scaffold splitting for the evaluation configuration.

reason.text: The loader reads this CSV as the dataset file.

unknowns: The source recommends scaffold splitting but does not establish that every other split is invalid; do not generalize this rule to unrelated datasets.

decisions.when: Evaluating a structure-to-solubility model on Delaney ESOL.
decisions.requires: The Delaney CSV and a plan for train, validation and test separation.
decisions.choose: Use the loader's scaffold split as the default comparison setup.
decisions.avoid: Silently replace the recommended split with a different split while comparing reported results.
decisions.because: The supplied Delaney loader explicitly recommends scaffold splitting for this dataset.
decisions.check: Record the split choice and verify that the target is measured log solubility in mols per litre.
decisions.stop_or_fallback: If the CSV or label column is missing, restore the pinned dataset before evaluation.
decisions.scope: Delaney ESOL model evaluation, not a universal rule for all chemistry datasets.

citations.quote: Scaffold splitting is recommended for this dataset.
